name: duel_ybot
_prefilter_note: the roundhouse peaks over ~6 source frames; the default 7-frame landmark prefilter cost 5 deg of shin angle there (0.04 m of foot height). 5 costs 1.4 deg.

root_offset.comment: 0.20 m of extra room through the kick. Ramped across src 116-139 and 162-185, where he is already retreating 0.24 m of his own accord, so nothing slides: his support foot is planted from src 139 and a step change there would skate. Reads as making range before a head kick, which is what a fighter does.

the closing bind. These characters' arms are ~4% longer relative to their legs than the performers', so at a leg-scaled stage separation their fingertips cross while the arms swing out into the T-pose (3 frames, dest 255-257). The settled T-poses were always clear at 0.09-0.13 m; only the spread collided.

_root_scale_note: one stage, one scale: the initial separation and both travel distances must share a factor or the geometry does not close. 0.9715 is the mean of the two characters' leg/performer ratios (YBot 1.0102, Ninja 0.9328).
_stage_note: the attacker (grey shirt, screen-left). Stage marks are the performers' measured T-pose separation (1.941 m in camera space) scaled to these two characters' legs: 1.886 m, split either side of the origin.

plant.comment: T-pose, turn-in, guard. Feet shift within the stance and step in; both ankles stay under 0.22 m.
right foot lifts to 0.17-0.20 m driving the step into punch 1
right foot lifts to 0.21 m on the last punch
right roundhouse: right ankle 0.18 -> 1.09 m @ src147, left ankle stays 0.06-0.09

leg_pose.comment: sized against the real MESHES, not a capsule proxy. 0.18 restores the reference ankle trajectory to +/-0.035 m and still put the foot through the Ninja's head: these characters are thicker than the performers and the video itself only clears by ~2 cm. 0.37 is 0.18 (faithful) + 0.19 (clearance), the minimum that clears every frame together with root_offset.
